revision or for the class board.

## The sheet

::::::: {.el-sheet .column-page data-title="Style: telling styles apart by their features"}
:::::: {.el-grid}

::::: {.el-card}
#### Baroque (about 1600–1750)
<p>Bach, Vivaldi, Handel. Harpsichord, <strong>basso continuo</strong>, mostly strings; terraced dynamics; ornaments; often polyphonic.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-sound="harpsichord" data-bpm="96"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/16
K:D
V:1
d2fe dcBA TB4 A4|]
V:2 clef=bass
D,2F,2 A,2D2 G,2B,2 A,2C2|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Classical (about 1750–1820)
<p>Haydn, Mozart, early Beethoven. Piano; balanced 4 + 4 phrases; simple chords, <strong>Alberti bass</strong>; melody and accompaniment.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="120"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:C
V:1
c4 e2 g2|B4 c2 d2|]
V:2 clef=bass
C,G,E,G, C,G,E,G,|D,G,F,G, C,G,E,G,|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Romantic (about 1800–1910)
<p>Schubert, Chopin, Wagner. Big orchestra; huge dynamic range; <strong>chromatic</strong> harmony; long expressive melody; <strong>rubato</strong>; leitmotifs.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="66"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:3/4
L:1/8
K:Ab
"Ab"e4 c2|"Fm"f4 e2|"Db"_f4 e2|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Jazz and blues
<p>Swing, <strong>blue notes</strong> (3rd, 5th, 7th bent down), 12-bar blues, 7th chords, improvisation, walking bass, rhythm section and front line.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="132" data-style="swing"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:C
"C7"G2 _B2 c2 _B G|"F7"_E2 F2 G4|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Pop and rock
<p>Verse–chorus form, a memorable <strong>riff</strong>, guitars, bass and drums. Rock is usually louder and harder.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="112" data-style="rock"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:E
"E"E,2 G,A, B,2 A,G,|"E"E,2 G,A, B,2 D2|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Minimalism
<p>From the 1960s: Reich, Glass, Riley, Adams. Short patterns repeated, changing gradually; slow-changing harmony; phasing.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="140"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:C
c e g e c e g e|c e g a c e g a|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Musical theatre
<p>A story in songs, acting and dance. <strong>Overture</strong>; solo, duet and chorus numbers; <strong>recitative</strong>; book, sung-through and jukebox musicals. Bernstein, Sondheim, Lloyd Webber.</p>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Film music
<p>Fits the scene. A <strong>leitmotif</strong> returns with its character.</p><ul>
<li>Chase: fast, loud, driving ostinato</li>
<li>Horror: dissonance, building tension, stabs</li>
<li>Romance: strings, legato, rubato</li></ul>
:::::

::::: {.el-card .el-wide}
#### Check yourself
<div class="eq" data-set="style"></div>
:::::

::::::
:::::::

## Describing style

- Name the style, then give the features that told you: "Baroque: a harpsichord, a busy bass line and lots of ornaments".
- The periods overlap; Beethoven is the usual bridge from Classical to Romantic.

- The longer lesson, with fuller examples: [Elements 9: Style](elements-style.qmd).

## Works Cited

<!-- works-cited: written by scripts/works-cited.py -->
::: {.works-cited}
**For students**

"Alberti bass." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberti_bass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberti_bass). Lowest, highest, middle, highest; Classical era; Mozart K. 545.

"Basso continuo." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basso_continuo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basso_continuo). Chord instruments (harpsichord, organ, lute, theorbo…) and bass instruments (cello, double bass, bass viol, bassoon); figured bass.

"Blue note." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_note](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_note). Lowered 3rd, 5th and 7th; between a quarter tone and a semitone.

"Classical period (music)." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_period_(music)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_period_(music)). Classical roughly 1750–1820; Baroque c. 1600–1750; Romantic c. 1800–1910; melody over a subordinate accompaniment such as an Alberti bass.

"Minimal music." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimal_music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimal_music). US West Coast, late 1950s–early 1960s; Young, Riley, Reich, Glass, Adams; repetition, phase shifting, additive process, consonant harmony.

**For teachers**

Elements of Music. School handout, 10 pp., n.d. The source handout these lessons were built from; its order is kept. Corrections are listed in lessons/ELEMENTS-NOTES.md.
:::
